A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the three-stage TPV devices with the Type-II superlattices are promising for mid-infrared TPV applications, and the performance of the devices can be improved further by better photocurrent matching.
we have successfully demonstrated the feasibility of interband cascade TPV devices with Type-II band alignment and a relatively short cutoff at room temperature.

The main takeaway from our work is that
by using Type-II superlattices as the active region of the device, we can reduce the bandgap of the absorber while maintaining the cutoff wavelength of the device at the same time.
the Type-II superlattices are a good candidate material for low-bandgap absorbers in TPV devices.

the use of superlattice absorber layers with relatively narrow bandgaps can be used to achieve higher values of open-circuited voltage at a given temperature, which is an important factor in the design of thermophotovoltaics for space applications.
